title: What Qualifies You as an Expert
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Distinguishes experience from expertise: people with long experience are not necessarily skillful until they become expert. The author says experts turn information into working knowledge by describing situations precisely and observing how choices lead to outcomes. What defines the expert is the accuracy of these cause-and-effect understandings, which lets them pick out the salient facts and predict how situations will unfold. Those who command facts without predictive ability are knowledgeable but not expert. The post closes with a practical path: sharpen your judgment about which factors matter, use them to see causal relationships, and let the accuracy of your predictions build your reputation.
points: Experience only creates the opportunity to learn; it does not guarantee that a person recognizes which information matters.
Expertise is defined by the accuracy of presumed cause-and-effect relationships between choices and outcomes.
True experts gather only the facts that yield new insight and ignore irrelevant ones, unlike the facts-collector who is merely knowledgeable.
Growth in expertise comes from improving the accuracy of predictions about the consequences of choices in unfolding situations.
quotes: Yet, we can all point to people with lengthy experience who are not very good at what they do. People with experience don’t become more skillful until they become more expert.

Over time, they gather practical information they can use to their advantage. While experience gives people the opportunity to collect insightful information, it doesn’t guarantee they will capitalize on the opportunity or even recognize what information matters.

By continually examining how situations unfold, soon-to-be experts begin to see causal relationships between choices and outcomes. It is the accuracy of these presumed cause-and-effect relationships that make them expert.
Experts don’t just collect information and facts and apply them. Rather, they know what superior information and facts are worth gathering and use them to predict how situations develop.

As your predictions about the consequences of any choice in an unfolding situation increase in accuracy, your expertise will grow with it. Once people learn of your predictive prowess, your reputation as an expert will grow as well.
